thread:
mohit: quick check — onboarding elmwood-9b landed upstream yesterday. license attached says 'Academic-Research-Only (ARO) v0.9'. we were planning int8 quant + staged perf tests. allowed to host or ship quantized weights? :thinking_face:
emily: my quick read: ARO usually blocks commercial hosting. looping in legal.
raj: ran some quick int8 runs this AM: latency -18%, throughput +22%. quality change small: MMLU fp16 74.3 -> int8 73.1 (~-1.2). snippet: `scripts/bench run --model elmwood-9b --quant int8`
mohit: pasted license excerpt below for context:
"Academic-Research-Only (ARO) v0.9
You are granted a license to use the Model for non-commercial academic and research purposes only. Distribution, sublicensing, and providing access to the Model as a service are prohibited without prior written consent from the Licensor."
anna (legal): thanks. that clause is pretty explicit: "providing access to the Model as a service are prohibited". this precludes hosting a public API or any customer-facing endpoint. Dedicated reserved capacity where customers access the model = also not allowed.
anna (legal): options: 1) request a commercial/hosting waiver from upstream; 2) keep model for internal R&D only under our internal controls (no external access); 3) require customers to obtain direct license from upstream and we operate only as integration engineers (ugh).
raj: for now i can keep the quant tests in our internal R&D VPC and tag the model as research-only in the registry. i already set up a private test endpoint bound to the onboarding project group (no internet egress).
legal-bot: created ticket LIC-2026 to contact upstream for hosting/commercial permission, assigned to anna.
emily: action items: stop any hosted rollout, mark elmwood-9b RESEARCH_ONLY in model catalog + UI badge, add quant/eval artifacts to onboarding PR, legal to pursue LIC-2026.
mohit: copying eval artifacts to the onboarding PR and reverting any hosted config.
ml-onboarding-bot: model registry update: elmwood-9b status=RESEARCH_ONLY ticket=LIC-2026 updated_by=mohit
anna (legal): one nuance to ask upstream: sometimes maintainers allow distribution of quantized artifacts or provide an explicit exception for non-commercial hosted evaluation. but the license language covers "providing access as a service" so we need express written permission to host. i'll ask about quantized derivatives specifically in LIC-2026.
raj: if they permit hosting of quantized weights, we can bake int8 artifacts into the model bundle and ship with a note about permitted usage. perf looks promising.
emily: until legal confirms, do not enable any public endpoints (embeddings or generation). internal experiments with access controls are OK.
mohit: understood, rolling back hosted routes now. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
